name: Memphis Grizzlies
headline: The Grizzlies are 6-2 with a +10.7 net rating, but two straight losses have ended the perfect start.
good: The offense is humming at 120.5 points per game with a 116.3 offensive rating, and they shoot 40.1 percent from three.
They win the glass and take care of the ball on defense, outrebounding opponents 49.2 to 42.5 and allowing just 109.8 points per game (105.9 defensive rating).
Ty Jerome is carrying the scoring load with 27.4 points on 62.6 percent true shooting and a 33.1 percent usage rate. Cameron Boozer adds 16.8 points, 9.8 rebounds and 5.4 assists as a rookie.
The bench is productive: Isaiah Stewart shoots 66.7 percent for 11.9 points in 18.3 minutes, and Cam Spencer has 5.8 assists in 19.8 minutes.
bad: Back-to-back losses at home: 135-134 in overtime to New Orleans and 107-103 to Indiana, after a 6-0 start.
Boozer is shooting only 37.3 percent from the field (53.2 percent true shooting) while turning it over 3.1 times a game, and Jerami Grant is at 38.2 percent with a 50.4 percent true shooting mark.
Memphis commits 15.5 turnovers per game versus 14.5 for opponents, and its 134 points still were not enough against New Orleans.
fans: The mood is a mix of surprise and caution. Local coverage called the 5-0 start a surprise led by Boozer and Jerome, and ESPN's Windhorst and MacMahon are discussing the staying power of Memphis in their league insider piece. The Pelicans loss stung because Jerome scored 40 and Memphis still lost its unbeaten mark by one point.
outlook: Memphis hosts Oklahoma City tonight at FedExForum in NBA Cup group play. The Thunder are also 6-2 and are 4.5 point favorites per DraftKings, and the over/under is 223.5. Our model gives Memphis about a 47 percent chance, so this is a good test of whether the early success holds up.
